memory_candidates.content: When sourcing agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/task-type-detect.sh's detect_task_type for a new extension's keyword_overrides, pass the real agent-system/extensions directory as the third argument (not the default .claude/extensions) to test against the extension's source-store manifest before it is ever deployed: `detect_task_type "$desc" specs/state.json agent-system/extensions`. Step 1 strong anchors (meta and lean4) resolve before any extension's keyword_overrides is ever read, and are structural: a lean4 strong anchor (the regex \.lean\b or the literals mathlib/lean4/mathlib4) captures a task unconditionally regardless of what a later-loaded extension declares. Step 2's keyword_overrides scan is alphabetical-directory-order first-match-wins and final (never remapped by step 5's alias pass), so a new extension sorting early alphabetically scans before most others and an over-broad token risks capturing their tasks.

check-extension-docs.sh refuses to run from the agent-system source-store path (it resolves ../.. to a bogus repo root from inside extensions/core/scripts/) -- it must be invoked as the already-deployed .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh (or .opencode/scripts/ equivalent) copy, confirmed by the script's own error message pointing at this. The same applies to validate-index.sh and validate-wiring.sh when checking a newly-authored, not-yet-deployed extension: run the deployed copies even though the extension itself lives only in the source store; an uninstalled extension produces INFO/WARN (not FAIL) for its routing targets, which is the expected, non-blocking signal.
